name: Mulldrifter
oracle_text:
Flying
When this creature enters, draw two cards.
Evoke {2}{U} (You may cast this spell for its evoke cost. If you do, it's sacrificed when it enters.)
blocked_sentences: Evoke {2}{U} (You may cast this spell for its evoke cost. If you do, it's sacrificed when it enters.)

needs.what: A card-level alternative cost that REPLACES the printed mana cost while casting from hand, so legality offers Mulldrifter twice: once for {4}{U} and once for {2}{U}. Shaped like the existing `kicker` field (a card-level cost string plus a flag on the cast action), but subtractive rather than additive, and it must leave the printed mana value at 5.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `kicker` is the only card-level mana cost besides `mana_cost`, and it is explicitly an ADDITIONAL cost paid on top - legality offers the card unkicked then kicked at mana_cost + kicker, so writing `kicker: "{2}{U}"` would make the evoked mode cost {6}{U}{U}, i.e. strictly worse, not cheaper. `cost_reduction` is generic-only, clamped at zero, read off the board every time and not a choice the caster makes, so it can neither cut the {U} pip nor be declined. `suspend` casts for free but only after exiling the card and waiting out time counters, and `retrace` only widens the zone a card may be cast from while adding a discard; neither replaces the mana cost of a cast from hand.

needs.what: A condition readable from the card's own effects that asks whether this permanent was cast for its evoke cost - the exact analogue of `{"kicked": true}` - so the enters trigger can sacrifice the creature only in that case. The flag has to survive the cast-to-battlefield zone change, since the question is asked when the permanent enters and by then the spell is gone.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `{"kicked": true}` is the only condition in the vocabulary that reads how a spell was cast, and the loader rejects it on any card without a `kicker` cost, so it cannot be borrowed for a different cast mode. The sacrifice half on its own is expressible - a `self_enters` trigger running `{"op": "sacrifice", "objects": {"self_only": true}}`, or the `may`-with-`else` idiom from "Sacrifice it unless you..." - but nothing can gate it on which cost was paid, so it would either always sacrifice (turning the {4}{U} mode into a strictly worse card than the one printed) or ask the caster a free yes/no they would always decline, which is the evoke clause doing nothing.
